body:
hi there -

Please note that for your immediate needs, you can use any DBAPI module you like by making use of the "module" argument:

```python

>>> import sqlcipher3
>>> from sqlalchemy import create_engine
>>> e = create_engine('sqlite+pysqlcipher://:testing@/foo.db?cipher=aes-256-cfb&kdf_iter=64000', module=sqlcipher3) 
>>> c = e.connect()

```

for the change, I'm not yet comfortable with any of the packages here.   Clearly we want to drop pysqlcipher entirely and if the author is claiming that it can't be guaranteed against security issues, that means we have to eradicate it from the code entirely, otherwise it becomes a CVE on our end.   So at the very least, we would need to document the above solution for Python 2 at least, as I assume (though I can't tell) that sqlcipher3 is Python 3 only.

for sqlcipher3 I am not getting a clear picture on if this package intends to be maintained either and overall I would want the "sqlcipher" community to make it a little more clear what should be used:

1. the README is not present on the pypi page, it's blank: https://pypi.org/project/sqlcipher3/
2. the code seems to be mostly that of pysqlcipher but isn't a fork, it's a new repo that starts up two years ago, what's that about ?
3. the package lacks proper trove classifiers, e.g. Python versions
4. the pysqlcipher README announces that it's no longer maintained, it should name a successor and/or simply allow itself to be transferred to the sqlcipher3 maintainer.   pysqlcipher still comes up at the top of searches, has more stars, etc.
5. most importantly there's nothing in sqlcipher3's readme at https://github.com/coleifer/sqlcipher3 that discusses its origins or maintenance intentions.  
6. While the sqlcipher3_binary package installs for me, the source distro had a strange failure mode in that it failed to build, but then said that it "installed successfully" without any error; the package in fact failed to be installed at all. not sure what that's about, broken setup.py should be fixed to fail properly if dependencies aren't found

since this is a package with security considerations, the bar is considerably higher for us to hardcode it within the module, only to find out the package has become insecure two years ago because the maintainer walked away from it.

The "dbapi" method that you've modified in #5849 could be altered to not import *any* DBAPI at all and simply point users to the above calling form; that way SQLAlchemy does not introduce security vulnerabilities by hardcoding to a library that might fall into an insecure state while we weren't looking.

At the very least, for your PR in #5849 it should be emitting a warning when pysqlcipher is used and in 1.4 I would be comfortable moving to "explicit DBAPI required" mode, as we are still supporting Python 2 for the 1.4 series.

issue.title: pysqlcipher dialect fails in SQLAlchemy >= 1.4

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

issue.body:
When using the pysqlcipher with the following connection string:
'sqlite+pysqlcipher://:{passwd}@/{filename}?cipher=aes-256-cfb&kdf_iter=64000'
, it fails with:

engine = create_engine(
  File "<string>", line 2, in create_engine
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/deprecations.py", line 298, in warned
    return fn(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/create.py", line 653, in create_engine
    do_on_connect = dialect.on_connect_url(url)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sqlalchemy/dialects/sqlite/pysqlcipher.py", line 134, in on_connect_url
    passphrase = url.password or ""
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'password'

The reason is that on_connect_url "expects" url to be an URL object while it receives 'str' instead.
A fix will be submitted and linked to this issue shortly.
